meta._comment: GENERATED by design-system/tools/generate-catalog.php, from the same sources as components.generated.json. Do not edit by hand; run the generator. Nodes are keyed type:name (component, token, recipe, rule, legacy, file). Each edge is [from, type, to], with a fourth element of attributes when it has any. What pages and stylesheets reach changes with every page edit, so it is not stored: npm run ds:graph -- <name> --impact reads it live.

edgeTypes.draws-with: component -> token: a components.css rule for something the component renders names the token
edgeTypes.calls: component -> component: the helper, or a template it includes, calls the other helper
edgeTypes.instead-use: component -> component or recipe: its docblock says to use the other instead, and when (attrs.when)
edgeTypes.references: token -> token: the token's value names the other (attrs.mode when only a media mode does)
edgeTypes.replaced-by: token or legacy pattern -> token or component: the legacy thing and what to use instead
edgeTypes.covers: legacy pattern -> token: the token matches a legacy token pattern
edgeTypes.uses: recipe -> component: the screen recipe calls the helper
edgeTypes.mentions: rule -> anything: the rule's text in workshopr-design-system.json names it

legacy:--coach-*, --planner-*, --tips-*,.why: Per-app reds were unified under the five brand tokens. Category and mode tint ramps (-cat-N, -mode-*) are not aliases and stay.

legacy:--mainsite-*.why: Per-app reds were unified under the five brand tokens.

legacy:--phase-*.why: Phases are naming only since Red Unification (D1). Every --phase-* colour is an alias of a --brand* token; use the brand token its `use` names.

legacy:.activity-card.why: The old agenda activity card. ws_planner_card is the shared planner card with the sanctioned activity-type colours.

legacy:.btn-primary.why: Bootstrap-era button classes. ws_button renders .ws-btn with the brand gradient, sizes, loading and disabled states.

legacy:.empty-state.why: A per-page empty message. ws_empty_state renders .ws-empty-state with the shared icon, title and action layout.

legacy:.form-group.why: A hand-built label and field pair. ws_form_row (or ws_input with a label) ties the label, hint and error to the field for screen readers.

legacy:.modal-overlay.why: The hand-rolled overlay has no focus trap, no Escape handling and no shared sizes. ws_modal / ws_modal_start render .ws-modal with all three.

legacy:.template-card.why: A per-page card copy that drifts in padding and radius. ws_card draws from --card-padding and --card-radius.

rule:appScopedOverrides.rule: App-specific component overrides MUST use the app's body class scope

rule:componentExemptions.rule: Some app subsystems intentionally use bespoke CSS instead of ws_* components — do not flag their raw HTML as violations

rule:componentFirst.rule: ALWAYS use ws_* components before writing raw HTML

rule:cssArchitecture.rule: Follow the established CSS architecture for each app

rule:databaseAccess.rule: All database queries MUST use PDO prepared statements

rule:deprecatedCssClasses.rule: Legacy button classes are deprecated in favor of ws_button() / .ws-btn

rule:designSystemUpdates.rule: When CSS changes are made, update the design system documentation

rule:globalHeader.rule: Use the unified header, ws_header(), on every page

rule:iconLibrary.rule: Use Material Symbols Outlined for ALL icons

rule:newComponentProcess.rule: New UI patterns go in the design system, not inline

rule:noFrameworks.rule: Vanilla JS and CSS only — no React, Vue, Tailwind, or CSS frameworks

rule:phaseColors.rule: All apps use the unified mainsite red color family

rule:tokenFirst.rule: ALWAYS use platform tokens for all styling

rule:typography.rule: Headings use Fraunces, body uses Inter (or Source Sans 3 for older pages)

rule:writingStyle.rule: All user-facing content must follow the Workshopr writing style guide

token:--animate-fade-out.purpose: Duration and easing for an exit fade, as in transition: opacity var(--animate-fade-out). See motion.md

token:--animate-scale.purpose: Duration and spring easing for a scale-in, such as a popover opening. See motion.md

token:--animate-slide-up.purpose: Duration and spring easing for an entrance that rises into place. See motion.md

token:--app-bar-height.purpose: Bar below the global header. ws_app_bar already ships at this value.

token:--app-content-wide.purpose: The page grid's full width: the content column of an /app/ view in a 1440 window

token:--app-dock-height.purpose: The floating dock (ws_app_dock): its own height, and the room a shell's scroll region keeps clear beneath the last thing on the page while the dock is up — the height plus one --space-4 above and below it.

token:--app-grid-col.purpose: The page grid every non-bleed /app/ view sits on: eight columns of --app-grid-col with --app-grid-gutter between them, 8×138 + 7×20 = 1244, the content column at 1440. Literal px, not calc(): the DTCG export and tests/header-shell.spec.js read these as plain strings. --app-grid-gutter is --space-5 by value; the alias is not written so the export stays flat.

token:--app-grid-gutter.purpose: The gutter between page-grid columns, and the gap of .app-page and every .app-grid-N

token:--app-rail.purpose: A shell rail is two columns of the grid: 138 + 20 + 138. Read by the app shell's .app-page placements and, inside the embedded tools, by the Planner palette and Synthesize material rails.

token:--app-rail-width.purpose: Leading side rail inside the tools, unified at Planner's width. The Facilitator console reads it for its agenda rail; Synthesize's standalone intake reads it too. The app shell's own rails are on the page grid below (--app-rail), which is a separate width by design.

token:--app-rail-width-compact.purpose: Narrow step for <=1024, matching Planner's existing breakpoint.

token:--backdrop-heavy.purpose: Dark scrim, heaviest, for a focus mode that hides the page

token:--backdrop-light.purpose: Dark scrim behind a panel or drawer, lightest

token:--backdrop-medium.purpose: Dark scrim behind a modal; --modal-backdrop uses it

token:--badge-border.purpose: ws_badge default border. Nothing reads it yet

token:--badge-text.purpose: ws_badge default text. Nothing reads it yet

token:--bg-cool.purpose: Cool Gray (Navigation, Drawers, Overlays) The --text-cool-* pair was deleted July 2026 (audit M8/D3): both were named as text tokens but measured 4.34:1 and 2.40:1 on white — below AA — and had zero consumers. Use --text-muted / --text-default for cool-surface text.

token:--bg-page.purpose: --bg-page is deliberately #FAFAF9, not the legacy warm cream #FEF7F1 — don't "restore" it. See DESIGN.md §7.

token:--bg-page-warm.purpose: Slightly warmer than --bg-page, used for immersive detail pages

token:--bg-paper.purpose: Standard grid/paper overlay background used in Planner, DNA, and Academy

token:--bg-paper-dark.purpose: Darker grid lines, panels, and borders for paper backgrounds

token:--bg-warm-muted.purpose: Warm muted background, midpoint between --bg-muted and --bg-page

token:--bp-desktop.group: SHARED: BREAKPOINTS (reference values ONLY — audit E1)

token:--bp-desktop-sm.group: SHARED: BREAKPOINTS (reference values ONLY — audit E1)

token:--bp-tablet-landscape.group: SHARED: BREAKPOINTS (reference values ONLY — audit E1)

token:--brand-ink.purpose: red text on white (5.02:1), headings, emphasis

token:--brand-line.purpose: borders and rules on a soft red fill

token:--brand-soft.purpose: chips, soft fills, the underline band

token:--brand-tint.purpose: the lightest wash: page bands, hover backgrounds

token:--button-bg-ghost.purpose: Ghost button fill. .ws-btn does not read it; Sidekick's .sk-btn--ghost does

token:--button-bg-secondary.purpose: Secondary ws_button fill. .ws-btn does not read it; only a Synthesize mockup does

token:--button-border-secondary.purpose: Secondary ws_button border. Nothing reads it yet

token:--button-radius.purpose: Button corner radius. .ws-btn does not read it; the planner's .btn (planner/index.php) does

token:--button-shadow-primary-hover.purpose: Shadow under a primary ws_button on hover

token:--button-text-ghost.purpose: Ghost button text. .ws-btn does not read it; Sidekick's .sk-btn--ghost does

token:--button-text-secondary.purpose: Secondary ws_button text. .ws-btn does not read it; only a Synthesize mockup does

token:--card-bg.purpose: Card surface: warm paper between --bg-paper (#FAF7F2) and --bg-paper-dark (#F0EBE3). White stays for modals, inputs and menus

token:--card-border.purpose: Card border, read by the ws_card family

token:--card-padding.purpose: 20px, which is what every page-level card already used before this token had any consumers: the workshop cards, the library listings, the build choices. It was declared at 24 and read by nothing, so the value moves to the one the cards are actually drawn at rather than the other way round.

token:--card-padding-compact.purpose: Dense cards — a draggable library row, a rail item — where 20px of padding would halve how many fit on screen. One step down, not a free-for-all.

token:--card-padding-roomy.purpose: Roomy cards: a full-width panel carrying a form or a settings section, where 20px against 840px of card reads as no inset at all. One step up, and the third and last member of this set. Settings drew --space-8 directly before this token existed, which is how its panels ended up outside the card family without anything noticing.

token:--card-radius.purpose: Card corner radius, read by the ws_card family

token:--card-shadow.purpose: Resting card shadow; app card styles read it, .ws-card does not

token:--color-auth-primary.purpose: Auth / login UI reds (auth-modal.css, styles.css, admin.css)

token:--color-error.purpose: Error status for icons, invalid-field borders and fills. 3.76:1 on white, so error text uses --color-error-dark or --color-error-ink

token:--color-error-dark.purpose: Error text on white (4.83:1) and the heavier error border. Only 3.95:1 on --color-error-very-light; use --color-error-ink there

token:--color-error-ink.purpose: Dark red — text on error backgrounds

token:--color-error-light.purpose: Mid error tint for fills and the glow round an invalid field. Text on it uses --color-error-ink (5.57:1)

token:--color-error-very-light.purpose: Palest error fill, an error row or panel. Text on it uses --color-error-ink (6.6:1)

token:--color-info.purpose: Info status for icons and fills that carry no text. 3.68:1 on white, so info text uses --color-info-dark

token:--color-info-dark.purpose: Info text and icons on white (5.17:1). Only 4.24:1 on --color-info-very-light; use --color-info-strong there

token:--color-info-light.purpose: Mid info tint for fills and borders

token:--color-info-very-light.purpose: Palest info fill, an info row or panel. Text on it uses --color-info-strong (7.15:1)

token:--color-ink-faint.purpose: ⚠️ 2.52:1 on white, 2.41:1 on --bg-page — decorative only, never essential text

token:--color-ink-faint-accessible.purpose: 5.39:1 on white, 4.80:1 on --card-bg: use instead of --color-ink-faint for essential text

token:--color-ink-muted.purpose: Stone hue (25deg, 5% saturation) at the lightest step that clears AA on every surface it sits on: 5.39:1 on white, 5.16:1 on --bg-page, 5.04:1 on --bg-paper, 4.80:1 on --card-bg, 4.54:1 on --bg-paper-dark / --header-bg. Was #78716C (4.28:1 on --card-bg) until Oct 2026

token:--color-orange-600.purpose: Status / icon accents (used in styles.css, admin, _modals.css)

token:--color-primary-on-white.purpose: 5.02:1 — use instead of --mainsite-primary for text on white

token:--color-purple-100.purpose: Pastel card-header gradient stops (styles.css, _modals.css). The -200 steps were deleted July 2026 (D3) — zero consumers.

token:--color-slate-900.purpose: Cool slate (dark tooltip / chip on light UI)

token:--color-success.purpose: Success status for icons, dots and fills that carry no text. 2.28:1 on white, so success text uses --color-success-ink or --color-success-darker

token:--color-success-dark.purpose: Heavier success icon or border. 3.30:1 on white: large text and icons only

token:--color-success-ink.purpose: Dark emerald — text on success backgrounds

token:--color-success-light.purpose: Mid success tint for fills and glows. Text on it uses --color-success-ink (6.34:1)

token:--color-success-very-light.purpose: Palest success fill, a success row or panel. Text on it uses --color-success-ink (7.0:1)

token:--color-teal.purpose: Teal — planner secondary action (e.g. launchpad button)

token:--color-warning.purpose: Warning status for icons, dots and fills that carry no text. 2.15:1 on white, so warning text uses --color-warning-ink

token:--color-warning-dark.purpose: Heavier warning icon or border. 3.19:1 on white: large text and icons only

token:--color-warning-ink.purpose: Dark amber — text on warning backgrounds

token:--color-warning-ink-dark.purpose: Darker amber — headings on warning backgrounds

token:--color-warning-light.purpose: Mid warning tint for fills and borders. Text on it uses --color-warning-ink (5.69:1)

token:--color-warning-very-light.purpose: The highlight fill. Was #FEF3C7 (amber-100) until Sep 2026. Text on it uses --color-warning-ink; --color-warning-darker falls to 4.32:1 and fails AA.

token:--divider-strong.purpose: A divider that has to read clearly, a step darker than the default border

token:--ease-reveal.purpose: Page-reveal regime (motion P1) — /motion.md's canonical values, tokenized. For landing/marketing scroll reveals and hero sequences ONLY; UI micro-motion uses the durations above. See motion-system.md.

token:--ease-spring.purpose: Organic settle — pure deceleration, does NOT overshoot despite the name

token:--exercise-light.purpose: Mid exercise fill and border; clipped into sRGB, so about 4% less saturated than its red. Text on it uses --color-info-strong (6.18:1)

token:--exercise-very-light.purpose: Palest exercise fill, an exercise row or panel. Text on it uses --color-info-strong (7.23:1)

token:--focus-ring.purpose: The whole ring as one value: outline: var(--focus-ring)

token:--focus-ring-color.purpose: The keyboard focus ring. Sky blue on purpose (decision D2): the one non-red accent, so focus is unmistakable. Keep it opaque; forced-colors mode swaps in Highlight

token:--focus-ring-halo.purpose: Soft outer glow, for components that pair a ring with a halo. Alpha is fine here because it is decorative — the opaque ring above carries the contrast obligation.

token:--focus-ring-offset.purpose: Gap between a control's edge and its focus ring

token:--focus-ring-width.purpose: Focus ring thickness; 3px under prefers-contrast: more

token:--grid-line-color.purpose: Standard signature drafting grid-paper overlay line color

token:--grid-min-lg.purpose: Wide cards with a paragraph or an image: ws_grid min lg

token:--grid-min-sm.purpose: Compact tiles and stats: ws_grid min sm. Also the floor a growing ws_cluster item keeps before its row wraps

token:--header-bg.purpose: The global header (ws_header) sits a step deeper than the page cream so the chrome reads as a distinct band rather than bleeding into content. Same value the apps already call --color-paper-dark.

token:--icebreaker-light.purpose: Mid icebreaker fill and border. Text on it uses --color-success-ink (5.54:1)

token:--icebreaker-very-light.purpose: Palest icebreaker fill, an icebreaker row or panel. Text on it uses --color-success-ink (6.42:1)

token:--icon-lg.purpose: The smallest an icon is anywhere (DESIGN.md §8), an SVG from icon() or a font glyph

token:--icon-md.purpose: Retired for icons: an icon is at least --icon-lg (DESIGN.md §8). Kept only because the native apps mirror it; never size an icon with it

token:--icon-sm.purpose: Retired for icons: an icon is at least --icon-lg (DESIGN.md §8). Kept only because the native apps mirror it; never size an icon with it

token:--icon-xs.purpose: Retired for icons: an icon is at least --icon-lg (DESIGN.md §8). Kept only because the native apps mirror it; never size an icon with it

token:--input-placeholder.purpose: Input placeholder text: decorative, never the label

token:--input-ring.purpose: Soft glow round a focused input

token:--link-hover.purpose: Link colour on hover. Nothing reads it yet

token:--link-visited.purpose: Visited link colour. Nothing reads it yet

token:--mainsite-gradient.purpose: The light stop is #D13A3A, not the brand #E54D4D. White on #E54D4D is 3.82:1, and this gradient backs --button-bg-primary, whose label is --text-small (11.2px at the 80% root, so normal text with a 4.5:1 bar). #D13A3A measures 4.80:1 and the dark stop 5.02:1, so the whole sweep now passes AA. Do not "restore" the light stop to #E54D4D: that reintroduces a Level AA failure on every primary button. Flat brand red is unchanged and still lives in --mainsite-primary. See AUDIT-2026-08-23-system-audit.md P1-2.

token:--modal-border.purpose: Modal border. Nothing reads it yet

token:--overlay-heavy.purpose: White veil over content, almost opaque

token:--overlay-light.purpose: White veil over content, lightest: the most of what is underneath shows through

token:--overlay-medium.purpose: White veil over content, for a frosted panel or a loading cover

token:--paper-grid-image.purpose: The drafting grid as one value, so it travels with the paper instead of being re-typed. Apps that override `body { background: ... }` wipe background-image with the shorthand — that is how five pages silently lost the grid. Set background-image: var(--paper-grid-image) alongside.

token:--planner-blue.purpose: Legacy "plan blue" aliases — retired under Red Unification. Repointed to the Learn Red family so any component still theming off --planner-blue renders red (planner pages already override these in css/planner/base/_variables.css; this keeps pages that load only the platform tokens, e.g. planner/index.php, in step).

token:--planner-gradient.purpose: Aliased rather than restated: this was a byte-identical copy of --mainsite-gradient, so it silently kept the 3.82:1 light stop when that one was corrected. One definition, one place to fix.

token:--space-7.purpose: added Sep 2026: 5 call sites across app-shell, stsh-shell

token:--text-dark.purpose: Headings and primary text: titles, labels, the main line of a card. 15.3:1 on white

token:--text-default.purpose: Body copy and descriptions. 7.66:1 on white

token:--text-faint.purpose: Decorative only: placeholders and disabled text, never information. 2.52:1 on white; prefers-contrast: more swaps in the accessible value

token:--text-muted.purpose: Secondary text: meta lines, hints, timestamps. AA on every surface: 5.39:1 on white, 5.16:1 on --bg-page, 5.04:1 on --bg-paper, 4.80:1 on --card-bg, 4.54:1 on --bg-paper-dark

token:--toast-bg.purpose: Toasts / Notifications Toasts are a deep-red surface with inverse ink (10.9:1), not a white card — the old --toast-bg: var(--bg-surface) never matched what shipped. #7F1D1D is red-900, promoted here as a real value per the theming rule (layer 3 may hold a value; app CSS may not invent one).

edges.when: for an activity inside the Planner, on the timeline or in the palette.
when the list is not an agenda: a stack spaces arbitrary parts.
for the steps the run took rather than the rules it met.
for a marketing list of what something includes.
for tasks the person works through themselves.
when the decision can wait beside the work instead of blocking it.
for one activity the person can add from a list of recommendations.
for the run's history once it is done, with details and a summary row, rather than live progress.
when the work has a known percentage.
when the wait is for data, not for the AI.
for the results of checks rather than the steps of a run.
for live progress rather than the record of a run.
when the mark needs words beside it: ws_badge('Prepared by Workshopr', ['variant' => 'ai']) carries the mark and says who made it.
for a full-width notice about the site or session at the very top of the page.
when the region loaded and is simply empty; empty and broken are different messages.
with its error option for one field's validation message.
for a transient confirmation that needs no acknowledgement.
when the message is about one region or action on the page rather than the whole site or session.
when it is the page's own headline and call to action; the hero renders the page's h1.
for a transient confirmation of something the user just did.
when the card is a route the reader picks to start a task rather than something to read.
for three to six parallel capabilities in a marketing grid.
for library records (exercises, workshops, icebreakers) that link to a detail page and carry favourite, notes and share.
for an activity inside the Planner, on the timeline or in the palette.

for the person's own saved workshops inside /app/ (Plan, Facilitate, Synthesize): it reads their rows and brings stages, views and the card menu. Outside /app/, or where there is no database, build the list from ws_card as recipe:filtered-workshop-list does.
when the cards are read side by side rather than peeked at as a stack.
for one recommendation shown whole, with its reason.
for a plain container.
when you are listing records (a saved workshop, an exercise) rather than offering routes.
when the pick is a value a form submits later rather than an action that starts at once.
for a search field with filters and their chips above a list.
when each item takes the full width, one above the other.
when the decision is inside a flow the person is already in, not a stop on the way somewhere else.
for a setting that only changes Workshopr itself.
for deleting something for good.
to space the parts inside the container; a container sets width only.
with the error variant when the request failed.
while the data is still loading, or the reader will think their content is gone.
repeated by hand with plus signs between: the formula keeps every tile the same width and hides the plus signs from screen readers.
for an exercise shown as one step of a recipe, where the step's minutes, not the exercise's own duration, are what matter.
with type search for a search field inside a form about something else, or in the site header rather than above a list.
for the whole list page: the filters with their results and the loading, empty and error states.
when the content is a single string.
for short items in a wrapping row that should keep their own widths.
for one column of items, each the full width.
for a site-wide notice across the top of the page rather than the page's headline.
on an interior or detail page, which needs an h2 or h3 rather than a second h1.
on a registered section page (home, library, academy, tips, planner), whose hero content lives in section-hero.php.
when the icon opens a list of actions, such as the three dots at the end of a row or card.
for a search box above a list, with or without filters: it brings the search landmark, the submit and the chips for applied filters.
with the segmented variant when each option is a different URL: tabs announce panels that switch in place, which a reload is not.
for a container that is not a library record.
when clicking the card starts a task rather than opening a record.
for the same record inside the Planner.
for a person's own saved workshops inside /app/: those are their plans, not library records, and carry no favourite or share.
for a person's own workshops outside /app/, searched and filtered, built from ws_card.
when there are only one or two actions: show them rather than hide them behind a trigger.
for the site's own navigation, workspace switcher and account menu, which the header draws.
when the reader picks a value a form submits, not an action or a page to go to.
when the choices need a search, a form or more than about ten entries.
on a workshop list card, whose menu carries the row's facts and routes until it moves onto ws_menu.
when the message belongs in the page beside what it is about, such as a validation summary or a failed load.
when the work runs alongside the page and the reader needs both at once, such as comments beside an agenda. It neither traps focus nor makes the page inert.
when an action is done and needs no decision (saved, copied): wsToast() confirms and goes away on its own.
for the whole delete flow: the danger button, the confirmation, the busy state and a failure that keeps the dialog open.
for a container that is not an agenda activity.
for the same activity in the library, outside the Planner.
when the activity is recommended with a reason rather than placed on the agenda.
when the choices are a handful of named options rather than points on a scale.
when the value moves in fixed steps the reader counts (seats, rounds) and should see as a number.
for a live countdown: a stat tops out at h2 size and has no timer semantics or states.
when the choices are actions to take or pages to go to, not a value a form submits.
when there is no score to give: that card grades a workshop, this one only draws its shape.
when the reader must finish or refuse something before going on, such as confirming a delete. The modal traps focus and makes the page behind it inert.
when there is nothing to work on, only a result to report.
when the region has finished loading and holds nothing.
when the work has a known percentage, such as an upload.
for a status or count.
for a topic or metadata tag.
when the items sit side by side and wrap: buttons in an action row, chips, a field beside its button.
when the items are repeated cards or tiles that should fill columns.
when several sections may be open at once, or each opens on its own.
for the content each tab shows: the row comes from ws_tabs, each panel from the pair.
for the heading of a page or a section, with its subtitle and description.
when the message must not be missed or concerns one region; an alert stays in the page until it is dealt with.
for a notice about the whole site or session rather than something the user just did.
when the user has to decide something before the page continues.
for library records that link to a detail page.
for a person's workshops outside /app/ or without a database, searched and filtered, built from ws_filter_bar, ws_card and ws_empty_state.
